rationale: The agent saw that test proteins also appear in training. It showed that one-hot protein identity lifts AUROC from 0.65 to 0.85 through memorized propensities rather than generalisation, so it declined to report the inflated figure and proposed a protein-disjoint split. It counted shared proteins (40 and 43) but never measured the share of test pairs with a protein seen in training (~100%), and it didn't run the per-protein label-rate baseline (~0.82).
